draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Bicholim! Locals call it Divchal, and 5th-century CE copper plates already mention a place here called Dipaka visaya. Today it's a small town in the mining heartland of Goa.
draft.hungryLine: Bicholim is a working town rather than a tourist strip, so ask locals where they eat.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk about 16 minutes to neighbouring Carapur, a small census town next door.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Take it slow around town, Bicholim is about 30 km from the bustle of Panaji.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Bicholim only became Portuguese in the late 18th century, as part of the New Conquests, long after the coast.

tips.title: Say it the local way.
tips.body: In Konkani the town is Divchal, and you'll also hear it called Dicholi.

tips.title: Plan your trip from Panaji.
tips.body: Bicholim is about 30 km from the state capital, so budget time for the drive.

story.title: Named on copper
story.body: The Hiregutti plates of Bhoja Asantika mention a locality called Dipaka visaya. Historians identify it with today's Divchali or Dicholi.

story.title: The warlords' land
story.body: The area was ruled by an independent warlord, the PrabhuDesais of Sankhali, or Sanquelim. They held it until the Portuguese arrived.

story.title: A New Conquest
story.body: The Portuguese took Bicholim in the late 18th century. It became headquarters of one of the seven concelhos of the Novas Conquistas.

story.title: Mining heartland
story.body: Bicholim is now a municipal council town in Goa's mining belt. The 2011 census counted 16,986 people here.
